quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She said, 'I couldn't have done it without your encouragement.'
options: She told me she couldn't have done it without my encouragement.
She told me she can't have done it without my encouragement.
She told me she wouldn't have done it without my encouragement.
quests.correctAnswer: She told me she couldn't have done it without my encouragement.
quests.sentence: She said, 'I couldn't have done it without your encouragement.'
quests.hint: 'Couldn't have done' stays (past modal perfect). 'Your' → 'my'. 'Couldn't' ≠ 'wouldn't' - different meanings.
quests.explanation: 'Couldn't have done' is a past modal perfect expressing impossibility without help - it stays unchanged. 'Your' → 'my'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The HR manager asked, 'How long does it typically take to onboard new employees?'
options: The HR manager asked how long it typically took to onboard new employees.
The HR manager asked how long does it typically take to onboard new employees.
The HR manager asked how long it typically takes to onboard new employees.
quests.correctAnswer: The HR manager asked how long it typically took to onboard new employees.
quests.sentence: The HR manager asked, 'How long does it typically take to onboard new employees?'
quests.hint: 'Does take' → 'took'. Statement order. 'Typically' stays.
quests.explanation: Drop 'does'. 'Take' → 'took'. 'Typically' (frequency adverb) stays. Use statement word order.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The industry magazine said, 'Learn a new skill every year to stay competitive.'
options: The industry magazine advised professionals to learn a new skill every year to stay competitive.
The industry magazine advised professionals learning a new skill every year to stay competitive.
The industry magazine said learn a new skill every year to stay competitive.
quests.correctAnswer: The industry magazine advised professionals to learn a new skill every year to stay competitive.
quests.sentence: The industry magazine said, 'Learn a new skill every year to stay competitive.'
quests.hint: Imperative: 'advised + professionals + to + learn'.
quests.explanation: 'Learn' is an imperative → 'advised professionals to learn a new skill every year to stay competitive'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The suspect said, 'I wasn't there!'
options: The suspect denied being there.
The suspect denied to be there.
The suspect denied that he is there.
quests.correctAnswer: The suspect denied being there.
quests.sentence: The suspect said, 'I wasn't there!'
quests.hint: 'Deny' is followed by the gerund (-ing). 'Deny to be' and 'deny that he is' are both incorrect.
quests.explanation: 'Deny' must be followed by the gerund: 'denied being there'. 'Denied to be' is ungrammatical. 'Denied that he is' uses the wrong tense.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The journalist asked, 'Is the committee prepared to revise its decision?'
options: The journalist asked whether the committee was prepared to revise its decision.
The journalist asked is the committee prepared to revise its decision.
The journalist asked whether the committee was prepared to revising its decision.
quests.correctAnswer: The journalist asked whether the committee was prepared to revise its decision.
quests.sentence: The journalist asked, 'Is the committee prepared to revise its decision?'
quests.hint: 'Is prepared' → 'was prepared'. 'To revise' stays (infinitive form). Use 'whether'.
quests.explanation: 'Is prepared' → 'was prepared'. 'To revise' stays as an infinitive - 'to revising' is incorrect. Use 'whether'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The global strategy guide said, 'Engage with the local community when expanding into new markets.'
options: The global strategy guide recommended engaging with the local community when expanding into new markets.
The global strategy guide recommended to engage with the local community when expanding into new markets.
The global strategy guide said engage with the local community when expanding into new markets.
quests.correctAnswer: The global strategy guide recommended engaging with the local community when expanding into new markets.
quests.sentence: The global strategy guide said, 'Engage with the local community when expanding into new markets.'
quests.hint: 'Recommend + -ing' is correct. 'Recommend to engage' is incorrect in British English.
quests.explanation: 'Recommend' is followed by the gerund: 'recommended engaging'. 'Recommended to engage' is not standard - use 'recommended engaging' or 'recommended that companies engage'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She said, 'Looking back, I realize I made some poor decisions.'
options: She said that looking back, she realized she had made some poor decisions.
She said that looking back, she realizes she made some poor decisions.

quests.sentence: She said, 'Looking back, I realize I made some poor decisions.'
quests.hint: 'Realize' → 'realized'. 'Made' → 'had made'. 'I' → 'she'.
quests.explanation: 'Realize' → 'realized'. 'Made' (past simple) → 'had made' (past perfect). 'I' → 'she'. The participle phrase 'looking back' stays.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The scientist asked, 'Which approach is more likely to yield positive results?'
options: The scientist asked which approach was more likely to yield positive results.
The scientist asked which approach is more likely to yield positive results.
The scientist asked which approach would be more likely to yield positive results.
quests.correctAnswer: The scientist asked which approach was more likely to yield positive results.
quests.sentence: The scientist asked, 'Which approach is more likely to yield positive results?'
quests.hint: 'Is more likely' → 'was more likely'. Statement order. 'Would be more likely' is an over-shift.
quests.explanation: 'Is' → 'was'. Use statement word order. 'Would be more likely' is an over-shift - 'is' simply shifts to 'was'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The financial planner said, 'Avoid relying on a single source of income.'
options: The financial planner advised clients to avoid relying on a single source of income.
The financial planner advised clients to avoid to rely on a single source of income.

quests.sentence: The financial planner said, 'Avoid relying on a single source of income.'
quests.hint: 'Avoid' takes gerund. 'Avoid to rely' is incorrect. Imperative → 'advised + clients + to + avoid relying'.
quests.explanation: 'Avoid' must be followed by the gerund (-ing): 'avoid relying'. 'Avoid to rely' is ungrammatical.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The news report said, 'The talks have broken down and no agreement has been reached.'
options: The news report stated the talks had broken down and no agreement had been reached.

quests.sentence: The news report said, 'The talks have broken down and no agreement has been reached.'
quests.hint: Both present perfects shift to past perfect: 'have broken' → 'had broken', 'has been reached' → 'had been reached'.
quests.explanation: Both verbs shift: 'have broken down' → 'had broken down' and 'has been reached' → 'had been reached'. Both clauses must be updated.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The court asked, 'What evidence was presented to support the claim?'

The court asked what evidence has been presented to support the claim.

quests.sentence: The court asked, 'What evidence was presented to support the claim?'
quests.hint: 'Was presented' (past passive) → 'had been presented' (past perfect passive).
quests.explanation: Past simple passive 'was presented' → past perfect passive 'had been presented'. Use statement word order.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The innovation workshop said, 'Question assumptions and challenge the status quo.'
options: The innovation workshop encouraged participants to question assumptions and challenge the status quo.

The innovation workshop said question assumptions and challenge the status quo.

quests.sentence: The innovation workshop said, 'Question assumptions and challenge the status quo.'
quests.hint: Double imperative: 'encouraged + participants + to + question... and challenge'.
quests.explanation: Two imperatives → 'encouraged participants to question assumptions and challenge the status quo'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She said, 'I'll let you know as soon as I have more information.'
options: She said she would let me know as soon as she had more information.
She said she will let me know as soon as she has more information.

quests.sentence: She said, 'I'll let you know as soon as I have more information.'
quests.hint: 'Will let' → 'would let'. In time clauses with 'as soon as', 'have' → 'had'. Do not use 'would have'.
quests.explanation: 'Will let' → 'would let'. In time clauses ('as soon as'), the present shifts to past: 'have' → 'had'. 'Would have' is incorrect in time clauses.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The engineer asked, 'Has the prototype been tested under real-world conditions?'
options: The engineer asked whether the prototype had been tested under real-world conditions.

quests.sentence: The engineer asked, 'Has the prototype been tested under real-world conditions?'
quests.hint: 'Has been tested' → 'had been tested'. Use 'whether'. Statement order.
quests.explanation: Present perfect passive 'has been tested' → past perfect passive 'had been tested'. Use 'whether' and statement word order.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The financial advisor said, 'Plan for the unexpected by building an emergency fund.'

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The proverb says, 'Things aren't always what they seem.'

The proverb said that things aren't always what they seemed.

quests.hint: Proverbs express timeless truths. The present tense is retained. When 'says' is the reporting verb, no shift is needed.
quests.explanation: Proverbs and universal truths retain the present tense in reported speech. 'Says' (present reporting verb) confirms no backshift is required.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The HR consultant asked, 'How did the proposed changes affect employee morale?'

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She said, 'There isn't much time left, so we need to act quickly.'

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The NGO asked, 'What has the company done to reduce its carbon footprint?'

quests.sentence: The NGO asked, 'What has the company done to reduce its carbon footprint?'
quests.hint: 'Has done' → 'had done'. Statement order. Do not change simple perfect to continuous.
quests.explanation: 'Has done' → 'had done'. Use statement word order. 'Had been doing' would change the aspect from simple to continuous.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The project manager said, 'Set measurable objectives so you can track your progress.'

quests.explanation: 'Set' → 'to set'. In the purpose clause, 'you can track' → 'they could track'. 'Can' → 'could'. 'Your' → 'their'.
